papers.title: Residual Nonextensivity from WIMP Freeze-Out: A Phenomenological Memory Channel
papers.abstract: In this work we formulate the thermal decoupling, or freeze-out, of weakly interacting massive particle dark matter within a dynamical Tsallis framework. The parameter $q_\chi$ is promoted to a function of $x=m_\chi/T$, describing a relaxation toward extensivity that need not be completed before chemical decoupling. We adopt a sectorial approximation during freeze-out, with an extensive Standard Model bath, and specify the statistical weights and effective kinetic closure used for the dark matter abundance. The total derivatives of the equilibrium density contain the variation of $q_\chi$, which changes the rate at which the abundance must evolve to follow its instantaneous reference state. The residual value $q_\chi^{\rm fo}$ then provides the input for a phenomenological memory channel into the electron-positron and neutrino sectors, while photons remain extensive. We derive the corresponding chain rule terms in the radiation energy and entropy balances and formulate the photon-reheating problem without assuming that comoving electromagnetic entropy is automatically conserved when $q$ varies. The resulting construction connects the freeze-out history with the neutrino-to-photon temperature ratio and $N_{\rm eff}$. We discuss the physical motivation, closure assumptions, and conditions under which this description can be used, without presenting numerical results or observational fits.

papers.title: Probabilistic Causality from Graviton Fluctuations
papers.abstract: We compute the commutator of a scalar field minimally coupled to gravity at leading order in $G_N$. The commutator is operator-valued, with terms involving derivatives of Dirac deltas supported on the Minkowski light cone. When evaluated on classical/coherent graviton states, these terms ``bend" the support of the commutator in precisely the way required to recover standard causality on a classical curved spacetime. However, these terms are also associated with a variance and are thus a source of uncertainty in the causal relations between events. We quantify this effect for a thermal state of gravitons at temperature $T$. In the large-time limit, the uncertainty of the lightcone position is given by $$ \text{Var}(\delta x) =\frac{4G_NTt}{3}\, , $$ where $\delta x$ is the displacement from the classical lightcone at $|\vec x| = t$. We obtain this result by subtracting a universal vacuum contribution that is logarithmically UV divergent and subleading at late times.
papers.comments: 10 pages + appendices; v4: matching the published version, references added

papers.title: Weyl conformal geometry vs Riemannian geometry of Weyl gauge invariant (dressed) metric
papers.abstract: Weyl conformal geometry is the natural underlying geometry of gauge theories of Weyl group (of dilatations and Poincaré symmetry), such as Weyl quadratic gravity and its generalisation, Weyl-Dirac-Born-Infeld action (WDBI). These are local, Weyl-anomaly free (quantum) gauge theories of gravity. We describe Weyl gauge symmetry from a more familiar Riemannian view of Weyl gauge invariant dressed fields by the Wilson line of dilatations. Weyl geometry can then be seen as Riemannian geometry of non-local dressed metric ($g_{\mu\nu}^*$), at the "cost" of (gauge-induced) non-commutativity in the UV, due to Wilson line. Then Weyl quadratic gravity and WDBI actions of Weyl geometry, which are Weyl gauge invariant in $d$ dimensions, have the same expression in Riemannian geometry defined by $g^*_{\mu\nu}$. This is a non-local map and dual description of the two geometries and actions in the symmetric phase. Unlike for the metric, the equation of motion of Weyl gauge field ($\omega_\mu$) does not commute with the dressing of the metric. Quantum non-locality, in particular entanglement, and non-commutativity are (gauge-invariant) physical artefacts of "translating" (local) Weyl geometry and Weyl gauge covariance into our real-world Riemannian geometry of Weyl gauge invariant observables, and they are evidence of Weyl gauge symmetry. At lower energies, $\omega_\mu$ becomes massive, can decouple and Einstein-Hilbert action and commutativity are recovered. The case of a light $\omega_\mu$ is also discussed.

papers.title: A friendly phantom: Late-time AdS-to-dS transition and cosmological tensions
papers.abstract: We present Ph-$\Lambda_{\rm s}$CDM, a phantom-scalar realization within general relativity of the sign-switching cosmological-constant idea, $\Lambda_{\rm s}$CDM, in which a phantom scalar evolving on a bounded hyperbolic-tangent potential induces a smooth mirror AdS-to-dS transition in the late-time dark-energy density. The wrong-sign kinetic term, usually viewed as pathological, becomes the mechanism lifting the field from a negative- to a positive-energy vacuum-like regime. The construction also shows that the field can become repulsive while its energy density is still negative. The cosmology nevertheless remains controlled: total energy stays positive, the late-time attractor is de Sitter rather than a Big Rip, and the dynamics remain safely infrared. Ph-$\Lambda_{\rm s}$CDM thus offers a concrete late-time mechanism with the potential to address multiple cosmological tensions.
papers.comments: 12 pages, 3 figures; Honorable Mention in the 2026 Essay Competition of the Gravity Research Foundation; matches the version published in Int. J. Mod. Phys. D

papers.title: Nonlinear particle detectors across the Rindler firewall
papers.abstract: We investigate Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to composite observables of a quantum scalar field, including quadratic coupling to the field momentum and coupling to the local energy density. We develop a distributional framework for evaluating the corresponding detector response functions and apply it to detectors crossing the Rindler firewall. While we recover the finite response of the derivative-coupling model, we show that quadratic momentum coupling leads to products of distributions that do not admit a canonical, regulator-independent definition in the sharp-firewall idealization. The vacuum correspondence between the local energy-density and quadratic momentum responses motivates the conjecture that analogous difficulties may arise for energy-density coupling in the sharp firewall model. Within the sharp, pointlike composite-coupling model considered here, our analysis further suggests that these pathologies originate from the discontinuous severing of correlations across the Rindler horizon.

papers.title: Gravitational Waves as Thermodynamic Shear Excitations in Scalar-Tensor Gravity
papers.abstract: Can a propagating spin-2 mode participate in a local thermodynamic process without assigning an autonomous entropy or a unique local energy to the wave itself? We show that this occurs as a local thermodynamic work process in Jordan-frame scalar-tensor gravity, where a timelike scalar gradient defines an internal gravitational thermodynamic medium. Building on the first-order TT deformation-response relation, we identify the local shear power $\mathcal W_\phi=\pi_{ab}^{(\phi)}\sigma^{ab}$ from scalar-frame traction mechanics and show that its leading pure-TT contribution is second order, gauge invariant, and enters the exact scalar-sector energy balance. We further show that the same effective anisotropic stress controls the scalar-tensor modification of the tensor-friction term, so the local shear-work process is directly encoded in gravitational-wave propagation. In geometric optics the corresponding ratio of shear work to GR-normalized tensor energy is controlled by the running effective Planck mass, providing a local thermodynamic interpretation of the standard modified gravitational-wave luminosity-distance law. Finally, we extend this shear-excitation mechanism to nonminimally coupled scalars, metric $f(R)$ gravity, and viable luminal Horndeski theories, and identify the condition required for the same interpretation in more general tensor sectors.

papers.title: On the Separation Between the Brightest Cluster Galaxy and the Intracluster Light
papers.abstract: We present a model-based framework to define an aperture separation between the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) and the intracluster light (ICL). Using the intrinsic BCG and ICL components predicted by the semi-analytic model \texttt{FEGA25}, we determine, for each halo, the aperture radius that minimizes the bias in the recovered ICL mass. The optimal radius is obtained by balancing the BCG stellar mass lying outside the aperture with the ICL mass enclosed within it. At $z=0$, the optimal aperture in physical units increases with halo mass approximately as $r_{\rm cut}\propto M_{\rm halo}^{0.28}$, close to the expected virial scaling. When expressed in units of the virial radius, the aperture becomes nearly independent of halo mass, with $r_{\rm cut}/R_{\rm vir}\simeq 0.045$ at $10^{14}M_\odot$. Applying the resulting aperture prescriptions, we recover the intrinsic BCG mass to better than 8\% (lowest percentile), while the ICL mass is recovered with median values very close to unity, and an average scatter of $\pm 3\%$. Extending the analysis to $z=1$ and $z=2$, we find that the mass trends remain similar, with the slope and intercept of $r_{\rm cut}/R_{\rm vir}$ that stay stable. Robustness tests show that the inferred aperture is most sensitive to the ICL concentration and BCG size, but the main trends are preserved. Our results provide a physically motivated aperture definition for connecting observational BCG--ICL measurements to intrinsic model components.
papers.comments: 15 pages, 8+1 figures, data repository has changed

papers.title: Gravitational Memory Beyond Null Infinity through Finite-Distance Carrollian Screens
papers.abstract: We investigate gravitational memory beyond null infinity by studying finite-distance null hypersurfaces endowed with Carrollian geometry. We show that the intrinsic degenerate geometry, optical data, and null Brown--York tensor of a finite null screen define a quasilocal Carrollian dissipative system, providing a natural framework to characterize the residual geometric response after the passage of radiation. To make this construction explicit and compare it with the standard asymptotic description, we use Robinson--Trautman spacetimes as an exactly solvable radiative setting. For asymptotically flat Robinson--Trautman geometries, we transform the solution to Bondi gauge and extract the asymptotic data directly in terms of the Robinson--Trautman field. In the linearized sector, the Bondi shear is purely electric and produces the standard displacement-memory effect associated with the relaxation toward the final Schwarzschild geometry. We show that the leading large-radius tracefree component of the finite-screen memory reduces to the Bondi displacement memory, while finite-distance corrections retain additional focusing, embedding dependence, angular drift, Coulombic data, and near-zone information. Thus, Bondi memory emerges as the universal asymptotic projection of a broader quasilocal Carrollian response. Late-time screens approaching the final Schwarzschild horizon exhibit exponentially decaying non-isotropic Carrollian data, leaving only the isotropic null Brown--York stress. As a by-product, we construct the Robinson--Trautman solution with nonzero cosmological constant to second order in the radiative amplitude and use the holographic dictionary to study the associated energy fluxes and find that the resulting charge does not obey a universal monotonicity property.
papers.comments: 78 pages, 3 figures. Version published in PRD

papers.title: The silent dark sector: a field-theory approach to unified dark fluids with vanishing speed of sound
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel class of field-theory models that provide a unified description of the dark sector as a single perfect fluid with vanishing sound speed. These models also admit the interpretation of cold dark matter interacting with vacuum energy while avoiding any phantom behavior and including standard $\Lambda$CDM as a particular case. Built upon a single scalar field invariant under transverse diffeomorphisms, the framework naturally implements the constraints imposed in the so called mimetic models. We analyze a particular simple example exhibiting an effectively evolving dark energy and find that it can reproduce the DESI best-fit CPL evolution with the same number of free parameters.
papers.comments: V2: two references added, matches published version. V1: 22 pages, 4 figures

papers.title: The macroscopic precession model of quasi-periodic oscillations for rotating compact objects
papers.abstract: The relativistic precession model (RPM) interprets the twin kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) as geodesic frequencies of test particles orbiting in the spacetime of X-ray binaries hosting either a neutron star (NS) or a black hole. In several NS X-ray binaries, QPOs are well reproduced by effective geometries nearly degenerate with a Schwarzschild-de Sitter (SdS) spacetime, hindering independent determinations of the mass, the angular momentum and other observables. We propose how to solve this physical limitation by incorporating the effects of orbiting matter spin, culminating in introducing the macroscopic precession model (MPM). We treat the disk inhomogeneities as spinning test bodies governed by the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon (MPD) equations and obtain non-minimal spin curvature corrections to the azimuthal and the radial epicyclic frequencies. We perform Monte Carlo Markov chain (MCMC) fits, based on the Metropolis algorithm, and model eight NS X-ray binary sources. Our statistical analyzes show that the data select the internal structure of the accreting matter, without requiring corrections to Kerr and Schwarzschild spacetimes through the introduction of any correcting de Sitter phase. Physically, the MPM paradigm explains why an effective SdS-like structure could be statistically favored if spin is not employed, through non-minimal spin-curvature coupling, leaving unaltered the test particle hypothesis.

papers.title: Hermes - Towards an Optimal High-Performance Algorithm for Cosmic Statistics of Large Data Sets
papers.abstract: We present Hermes, an in situ multiresolution framework for efficient and flexible measurements of cosmic large-scale-structure statistics from discrete catalogues. Hermes replaces conventional ex situ counting of particle tuples with algebraic operations among window-filtered continuous fields. A discrete point distribution is first reconstructed as a continuous density field in a compact scaling-function representation, in which two- and higher-point statistics are formulated as spatial products of locally filtered fields. This formulation expresses conventional binning for counts-in-cells and two- and higher-point correlation functions through window functions. Changing the window kernels defines generalised statistics without redesigning the estimator. We further introduce PyHermes, an open-source Python implementation of this framework, combining multiresolution field reconstruction with FFT-based window convolution, MPI/thread parallelism, and GPU acceleration for high-order field contractions. The framework supports a broad range of measurements, including isotropic and anisotropic two-point statistics, marked correlations, standard and multipole three-point functions, filtered statistics, and Fourier-space differential operators for constructing derived physical fields. Using halo catalogues from cosmological N-body simulations, we demonstrate PyHermes through a range of clustering statistics and use benchmarks to quantify its computational efficiency and scalability for large-scale data sets. By separating field representation from statistical windows, Hermes provides a unified computational framework in which a single reconstructed field can be reused for a wide range of standard and customised cosmic statistics. This field-window architecture enables scalable analysis of the large data sets expected from current and future galaxy surveys.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society. 49 pages, 20 figures, and 4 tables. Source code: this https URL

papers.title: Modified Mukhanov-Sasaki equation and primordial perturbations in $κ$-deformed non-commutative space-time
papers.abstract: We study the inflationary primordial perturbations in $\kappa$-Minkowski non-commutative space-time, a Lie-algebraic type deformation of canonical space-time motivated by quantum gravity scenarios. Employing the $\kappa$-deformed star product formalism, we construct the bilinear action for curvature perturbations and derive the $\kappa$-deformed Mukhanov-Sasaki equation and obtain the perturbative solutions. Further, we compute the primordial power spectrum and spectral index, showing that the leading order corrections to the power spectrum induces scale-dependent term proportional to $(\ln k)^2$. The spectral index also exhibits an explicit $\ln k$ dependence, which persists even when the slow-roll parameters are constant. We also perform a Bayesian MCMC analysis using ACT DR6 data and constrain the $\kappa$-deformation length scale to $\lambda=1.93^{+1.88}_{-1.33}\times 10^{-29}m$ at $1\sigma$ CL, approximately four orders of magnitude larger than the Planck scale, demonstrating that the $\kappa$-deformed space-time offers a potential window into quantum gravity phenomenology through precision cosmology.

papers.title: Gravitational Wave Modeling of White-Dwarf--Compact-Object Binaries and Observational Outlook
papers.abstract: Binaries consisting of a white dwarf and a compact object (neutron stars, black holes, or sub-solar-mass compact objects) display unique orbital evolution and gravitational wave signals. We investigate the end stages of these systems by developing a novel integrator implementing mass transfer and 2.5-order Post-Newtonian kinematics. White-dwarf--compact-object binaries are subject to two phases: a slow inspiral during which binary evolution is dominated by weak-gravity radiation reaction and a quicker "outspiral" dominated by mass transfer. These systems have unique gravitational waveforms with several characteristic features including an accumulation of signal near the maximum cutoff frequency set by the transition between in- and outspiral. We investigate trends in gravitational wave parameters based on component masses. In particular, maximum cutoff frequency depends strongly on white dwarf mass and compactness. It is unlikely that extragalactic binaries will be measured by LISA or current or future terrestrial detectors. However, white-dwarf--compact-object binary end stages will be an important source for future decihertz detectors such as DECIGO and LGWA: The final inspiral of tens of white-dwarf--neutron-star binaries will be detected annually by LGWA, and millions of inspirals along with thousands of outspirals will be detected by DECIGO. The ultimate fates of these binaries are diverse and dependent upon the intricacies of angular momentum loss. In particular, we show that white dwarfs with partners of sufficiently low/high mass can end their lives in mergers, while white dwarfs do not enter contact with partners of intermediate mass. The highest frequencies produced by white-dwarf--compact-object binaries in our tests are 10--20 Hz--incapable of mimicking sub-solar-mass compact object signals in terrestrial detectors or explaining S251112cm-like signals.
papers.comments: 20 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D

papers.title: Inflation in unimodular loop quantum cosmology
papers.abstract: We study inflation in the setting of unimodular loop quantum cosmology, where time evolution is defined in unimodular time rather than with respect to a free, massless scalar field as is standard in loop quantum cosmology. The unimodular setting leads to a natural Schrödinger time evolution in a time coordinate with clear geometric meaning, defined independently of any particular matter content; an inflaton can be included but is not needed as a clock. We review the unimodular version of loop quantum cosmology and comment on possible connections to full (unimodular) loop quantum gravity. Then, focusing on semiclassical effective equations, we derive analytical solutions in simple cases such as a constant potential, emphasising the use of a unimodular time coordinate. We also discuss numerical solutions for phenomenologically interesting cases such as a quadratic potential and Starobinsky inflation, comparing different possible choices of initial conditions. In particular, we show that choosing an $\alpha$-attractor potential allows for models of a bounce either dominated by kinetic or potential energy, which are compatible with observations while potentially including observable imprints of the quantum-gravity regime.
papers.comments: 34 pages, 10 figures (with 30 figure files); Python code included as ancillary files; v2: minor changes in presentation following peer review. To appear in Classical and Quantum Gravity

papers.title: Stellar mergers and chemical element mixing: implications for metamorphic stellar evolution in AGN disks
papers.abstract: Chemical mixing during stellar mergers can significantly influence the subsequent evolution of the merger remnant. We perform a suite of three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations of stellar mergers, each evolved for $\sim100$ stellar dynamical times until the remnant reaches a quasi-hydrostatic equilibrium. The simulations incorporate subgrid-scale diffusion models to capture the turbulent mixing of chemical elements. Starting with an idealized polytropic equation of state (EOS), we first identify the dominant mixing mechanisms and investigate how the merger outcome depends on the mass ratio, relative velocity, impact parameter, and stellar structure. We then extend our simulations to the context of stars embedded in active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks, using a realistic, composition-dependent EOS and AGN stellar models generated with the stellar evolution code MESA. We find that mergers with both younger metamorphic stars and H-rich accreting AGN stars can substantially rejuvenate old metamorphic stars through efficient core mixing after thermal relaxation. The merger remnants are nitrogen-enriched, with ${\rm N/O}\sim1$--3 and ${\rm N/C}\gtrsim5$, comparable to the abundances observed in the nebula surrounding SN~1987A. During subsequent stellar evolution, the remnants may converge onto the main sequence of isolated metamorphic AGN stars once they reach accretion--wind equilibrium. They may also deposit a significant amount of chemically enriched material into the AGN disk. This work provides a physical framework for connecting hydrodynamical stellar mergers with the long-term evolution of AGN stars and their observational and chemical signatures.
papers.comments: Matching the version that was accepted to ApJ

papers.title: Primordial Correlators from a Kaluza-Klein Graviton Continuum
papers.abstract: Cosmological collider signals are usually discussed for isolated massive particles, whose exchange produces characteristic logarithmic oscillations in primordial correlators. In this work, we study how this signal is modified when the exchanged states form a continuous mass spectrum. We first develop a spectral representation for inflationary correlators mediated by a continuum field. In the soft limit, the non-analytic part of the seed function is expressed as a Fourier--Laplace transform of the spectral weight with respect to logarithmic momentum variables. This representation shows that a continuum superposes clock signals with different frequencies and can dephase the sharp oscillation associated with a single massive particle. We then realize this mechanism in an RS2-like inflationary braneworld, where the inflaton is localized on a de Sitter brane in a five-dimensional AdS bulk. The tensor sector contains a localized massless graviton and a continuum of Kaluza-Klein gravitons starting at \(m=3H/2\). We derive the KK wavefunctions and identify the brane spectral weight fixed by the continuum wavefunction on the brane. Applying this weight to the inflaton four-point function, we find a smooth seed function rather than a persistent logarithmic clock oscillation. This behavior follows from the fact that the continuum starts at zero clock frequency, while the KK spectral weight vanishes near threshold. Our results provide a concrete higher-dimensional example in which deviations from the standard cosmological collider signal encode the structure of a continuum high-energy spectrum.

papers.title: Quadratic effective energy--momentum tensor on uniform-density hypersurfaces during slow-roll inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate the quadratic-order effective energy-momentum tensor (2EMT) of scalar cosmological perturbations on uniform-density hypersurfaces during slow-roll inflation. The 2EMT is a gauge-fixed effective source rather than a gauge-invariant observable. We impose the complete scalar gauge conditions $\delta\rho=0$ and $E=0$, express all perturbations in terms of the Bardeen potential $\Psi$, and distinguish the strict infrared and ultraviolet limits from the intermediate regimes. The uniform-density time shift differs from the comoving one by an explicitly gradient-suppressed term, $Q_{\mathrm{UD}}-Q_{\mathrm{C}}=-\Delta\Psi/[3{\mathcal H}({\mathcal H}'-{\mathcal H}^2)]$. The two sources vanish at zero gradient, while their first nonzero infrared coefficients differ and give $w_{\rm raw}\simeq-1/3$ at leading slow-roll order. In the intermediate infrared, all four gauges have this leading ratio, with gauge-dependent amplitudes. In the ultraviolet, the longitudinal, spatially-flat, and comoving gauges give $w_{\rm raw}\simeq1/3$, whereas the uniform-density gauge gives $w_{\rm raw}\simeq1$. The common $1/\epsilon$ enhancement of the matter-clock gauges reflects the slow evolution of their clocks; the additional uniform-density $1/\sigma_2^2$ enhancement originates from the Laplacian contribution to the density constraint. Neither enhancement is interpreted as a gauge-independent physical instability, and the gauge reconstruction must remain perturbatively small.

papers.title: PowerFull: fast and accurate computation of the relativistic angular galaxy power spectrum including local primordial non-Gaussianity
papers.abstract: Current and forthcoming wide-field galaxy surveys, such as SPHEREx and Euclid, provide a unique opportunity to probe the ultra-large scales of structure formation, where primordial non-Gaussianity, often parameterized by $f_\text{NL}$, is expected to leave its most detectable imprint. At the same time, these surveys inevitably enter regimes where relativistic and wide-angle effects become significant, requiring careful modeling to extract unbiased cosmological information. We address these challenges by applying the total-angular-momentum (TAM) formalism to describe redshift-space clustering beyond the flat-sky approximation. The standard Fourier-mode description, which characterizes distortions by the angle between a mode and a line of sight, becomes ill-defined over wide fields, whereas the TAM basis naturally separates radial and angular contributions and incorporates the relevant relativistic effects. Within this framework, we provide a new parameterization of wide-angle predictions that can be compared directly with survey data. We then introduce PowerFull, a modification of the Julia-based 2-FAST package, which enables efficient computation of the full relativistic angular power spectrum. Finally, using Fisher information matrix-based analyses, we show that a survey like SPHEREx reaches $\sigma(f_\text{NL}) \sim 1$, but that neglecting the relativistic and wide-angle contributions shifts the recovered $f_\text{NL}$ by an amount of order its own uncertainty: at this precision the inferred value is biased unless the clustering is modeled consistently.

papers.title: Cryogenic Mechanical Loss of GaAs/AlGaAs Crystalline Coatings
papers.abstract: Optical coatings with minimal thermal noise are essential for high-precision, laser-based metrology experiments. Substrate-transferred crystalline GaAs/Al$_{0.92}$Ga$_{0.08}$As coatings have the lowest thermal noise for high-reflectivity mirror coatings with $\lambda =900$ nm -- 12 $\mu$m. Time-frequency stabilization experiments have demonstrated that GaAs/AlGaAs mirror coatings have a lower noise floor than amorphous mirror coatings. These mirrors are now being developed at sizes $\ge 300$ mm for gravitational-wave detectors. In order to understand the coating's fundamental loss mechanisms, which cause thermal noise, we have performed the first measurement of the mechanical loss at cryogenic temperatures using a cryogenic, multimodal, gentle nodal suspension system, which operates from 12 K to room temperature. This initial measurement used a silicon substrate whose asymmetry produced excess friction with the nodal support. Accounting for this friction and Akhiezer loss in the substrate and coating, the mechanical loss agrees well with the thermal noise observed in experiments using cryogenic fixed-cavities with GaAs/AlGaAs mirrors.
papers.comments: 10 pages, 11 figures, To be submitted to Physical Review D

papers.title: COSMOS-Web: From early star-formation enhancement to late suppression in galaxy groups
papers.abstract: Galaxy groups trace dense environments where interactions, gas removal, and reduced accretion may drive quenching. Common diagnostics trace star formation only over short timescales ($\lesssim100$ Myr), so time-resolved star formation histories (SFHs) are needed to separate recent changes from longer-term evolution at fixed mass and redshift. Using COSMOS-Web data, we test how group environment correlates with star-formation activity, and how this evolves with cosmic time and group-centric distance. We combine COSMOS2025/COSMOS-Web stellar masses and non-parametric SFHs with group detections and probabilistic memberships from AMICO. We compare stacked SFHs of group and field galaxies matched in mass and redshift, using the 30 richest groups in each redshift bin to measure how the SFH offset evolves with group-centric distance. Massive galaxies ($\log(M_\star/M_\odot)>10.5$) show the largest offsets but are already quenched in both environments. For lower masses ($8.1<\log(M_\star/M_\odot)<10.5$), suppression is clearest at $z<1$ (recent deficits of up to $0.7$ dex), while at $z>1$ SFHs show weaker suppression or occasional enhancement. The radial signal evolves similarly: quenching is broad across radius at low $z$, the inner--outer contrast appears at $z>0.5$, and any ordering at $z\gtrsim2$ remains tentative given growing uncertainties in the AMICO centroids. Groups are thus more mixed at early epochs, with both suppressed and occasionally elevated SFHs, while suppression dominates at $z<1$, most clearly for low-to-intermediate-mass galaxies. This fits a picture where inner-region galaxies spend more time in the group potential, undergo more passages through dense intra-group gas, and accrete less pristine cold gas, making quenching progressively clearer with cosmic time.
papers.comments: 14 pages, 11 figures. Revised version after first referee report, resubmitted to A&A

papers.title: A Unified Tracer Analysis of DESI DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillations
papers.abstract: We improve upon previous efforts to optimally combine overlapping galaxy samples in the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) analysis. By weighting each galaxy by its linear bias, overlapping galaxies are combined into a single, unified catalog, naturally avoiding double counting of cosmic volume and including all auto- and cross- information at the catalog level. Improvements over the previous effort include the addition of quasars out to $z=1.6$ to account for all overlapping DR2 tracers and redshift-dependent bias treatment to improve reconstruction. We report distance measurements using this unified tracer, and find them to be highly consistent with the baseline DR2 BAO analysis. We also test for tracer-dependent systematics within the DESI data, and find no evidence of tracer-dependent systematics within $0.8<z<1.6$. Finally, we take advantage of the unified tracer to rebin the analysis in redshift in order to more finely resolve the redshift-to-distance relation. Dynamical dark energy results on this finer redshift binning indicate that there is no missed feature in the expansion history in the redshifts $0.8<z<1.6$, and reproduces DESI's preference for an evolving dark energy equation of state.
papers.comments: 25 pages, 13 figures. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D

papers.title: Little Red Dots as Shock-Powered High-Energy Neutrino Sources
papers.abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact, high-redshift sources whose physical nature remains uncertain. Their optical spectra motivate a scenario in which their emission may be powered by shocks interacting with dense surrounding material. We investigate whether such interactions can power LRDs and contribute to the diffuse high-energy neutrino intensity measured by IceCube. In our simplified model, a fast central-engine outflow drives a shock through stationary or slow outflowing material, followed by a prescribed quasi-stationary interaction near the LRD photosphere. We consider the time-averaged neutrino emission from shock-active LRDs without requiring a single shock to persist throughout the LRD lifetime. We explore parameter ranges motivated by the observed and inferred properties of LRDs, finding solutions with shock luminosities 2.0e43 < L_s < 3.5e44 erg/s. Using an analytical framework for cosmic-ray acceleration and hadronic interactions in dense shock environments, we calculate the resulting high-energy neutrino emission and integrate it over the cosmological LRD population. For our fiducial cosmic-ray parameters, the average predicted contribution below 2e5 GeV increases from 0.2% for the lowest-luminosity quintile to 2% for the highest-luminosity quintile, while an illustrative higher-efficiency case reaches 13% of the IceCube diffuse neutrino intensity. These estimates assume all observed LRDs are shock-active. A smaller active fraction or a reduced covering factor would decrease the predicted intensity, whereas survey incompleteness could increase it. Improved models and population synthesis are needed to constrain the total LRD contribution.

papers.title: Stokes Phenomena between AdS/CFT and dS/CFT
papers.abstract: As parameters are varied, the set of saddle points contributing to a (path) integral may change discontinuously, leading to a corresponding change in the asymptotic expansion of the integral. This behavior is known as the Stokes phenomenon. We explore this phenomenon in the context of the analytic continuation problem relating the AdS/CFT and dS/CFT correspondences. In this paper, we study these correspondences for three-dimensional pure gravity and two-dimensional Liouville theory, using independent calculations in bulk minisuperspace and in the boundary Liouville zero-mode. In the bulk, the dS contour selects a single saddle and yields the tunneling wave function. Upon continuation to AdS, the contour instead selects an infinite family of saddles. The boundary calculation independently reproduces the same Stokes structure at leading semiclassical order, providing a nontrivial holographic consistency check. Our construction also offers a contour prescription for the conformal factor problem in Euclidean AdS$_3$ quantum gravity within minisuperspace.

papers.title: Regular Cosmologies: Three Distinct Routes
papers.abstract: Regular black holes avoid the central singularity by replacing it with a de Sitter core. We ask what cosmology follows if the same idea is brought to the early universe. Regular metrics define a position-dependent cosmological term, $\Lambda_{\rm eff}(r)=8\pi G \rho_{\rm MS}(r)$, and there is no unique way to carry it over to the expanding universe. We follow three different prescriptions: a Newtonian one following McCrea and Milne, a running vacuum evaluated at Hubble radius and a quasi-local one based on Misner-Sharp mass. We apply each of them to six regular black hole metrics and explore their consequences. In the Newtonian case the Friedmann equations are solved in closed form for the Hayward metric, and in terms of standard special functions or numerically for the others, and describe a universe that starts in a de Sitter phase and ends as dust (i.e. an inflationary model instead of dark energy). We find that in all three prescriptions a monotonically decreasing core density gives an equation of state that never crosses $w=-1$, and thus the phantom behaviour suggested by DESI would require a density shell which a regular core does not have. The three prescriptions agree on the de Sitter core but differ at late times, and we quantify the difference against the DESI DR2 results. We also point out that a single regularisation length cannot serve as both the inflationary and the dark-energy scale.
papers.comments: 34 pages, 4 figures. v2: revised, corrected and extended version. New section on the covariant origin of Newtonian route

papers.title: Tachyonic particle production in strongly supercooled phase transitions
papers.abstract: In strongly supercooled cosmological phase transitions, which generically lead to strong, observable gravitational-wave backgrounds, the scalar field typically transitions to a value well below the minimum of its potential. We study particle production caused by the subsequent evolution of the field. Because some modes feature temporarily tachyonic masses, they can be efficiently produced, and a significant fraction of the energy density released in the phase transition can get converted to particles rather than gradient energy. This has consequences for the shape and amplitude of the gravitational-wave spectrum caused by the interactions in bubbles and sources a new, high-frequency signal.
papers.comments: 9 pages, 4 figures. Fixed a numerical error, updated Figs 3 & 4 and their discussion

papers.title: Periastron advance from the perturbed Binet equation
papers.abstract: We apply the Poincaré-Lindstedt method to the perturbed Binet equation describing conservative dynamics of the perturbed Kepler problem. We show that a simple treatment of divergent terms directly determines the frequency shift of the radial motion and hence the periastron advance. We provide explicit expressions for polynomial, logarithmic and inverse power perturbations, extend the procedure to higher perturbative orders and to problems involving several perturbation parameters. Applying this method to different physical effects relevant to compact binaries, we recover known results. We also obtain new contributions to the periastron advance, including the leading-order effects of arbitrary mass- and current-type tidal multipoles and mass-type spin-induced multipoles, the NNLO current-type tidal quadrupole contribution, electromagnetic electric-dipole contributions to NNLO and the eccentric corrections to the electric charge. Finally, we illustrate how the method can be directly applied to the problem of particle motion in Reissner-Nordström, de Sitter-Schwarzschild metrics and in a Yukawa potential.

papers.title: Transient resonances of chaotic orbits in magnetized black hole spacetimes: an event-based frequency-ratio diagnostic
papers.abstract: The geodesic equations of the Kerr spacetime are separable, and this separability is what makes orbital dynamics around black holes tractable. An external electromagnetic field removes it, the motion turns chaotic, and the orbit wanders between resonances for irregular and unequal intervals; a long-time Poincaré section returns a single static blur, so that it records where an orbit has been but not when. We introduce the sliding-window frequency ratio, an event-based diagnostic that counts polar turning events within a window of fixed radial-cycle number and returns the local ratio of the two frequencies without any spectral decomposition; for regular motion with bounded count deviations, the error falls off as the window widens. We first establish that a single globally chaotic orbit in a magnetized black hole spacetime pays temporally ordered visits to distinct resonances, and that the corresponding section structure appears only in those intervals that the event counts select. A charged orbit in magnetized Kerr spacetime dwells near 3/5 and later near 4/7, opening fivefold and sevenfold structures, while a photon in Schwarzschild--Melvin spacetime holds 4/5 across a fivefold pattern. Because we keep every event time, we can replot each selected interval as its own section, and integer counts then agree with phase-space geometry. These visits control the phase accumulated along an orbit, and they therefore bear on any orbit-based probe of strong-field black hole geometry.

papers.title: Extremal black hole mimickers: geometry, stability, and long-delay signal trains
papers.abstract: We present a spacetime that serves as a horizonless mimicker of extremal black holes. Unlike previously studied mimickers of black holes with non-degenerate horizons, whose geometries are of the wormhole type and consist of two asymptotically flat regions connected by a very long throat, the mimicker of an extremal black hole possesses a single asymptotically flat region at one end and an infinitely long throat at the other. In the throat region, the spacetime approaches the direct-product geometry $M_{1,1} \times S^2$, where $M_{1,1}$ is two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime and $S^2$ is the two-sphere. We investigate scalar-field dynamics and the fate of the Aretakis instability. Although Aretakis-like modes arise in a local analysis of the throat, they do not lead to a physical instability of the mimicker. A scalar perturbation initially localized in the throat gives rise, at late times, to a sequence of signals with a characteristic separation $t_{\rm delay}\sim 1/\lambda$, where $\lambda\ll 1$ is a deformation parameter. This timescale is parametrically larger than the echo time $t_{\rm echo}\sim \ln(1/\lambda)$ characteristic of non-extremal black-hole mimickers. We refer to this sequence as a {\it long-delay signal train}. Geometrically, the periodicity of the long-delay signals is associated with periodic geodesics on $S^2$. We then extend the construction to extremal Kerr. In this case, the throat region approaches a generalized product geometry involving $M_{1,1}$ and a two-dimensional surface $\Sigma_2$. The corresponding signals are expected to form a quasi-periodic signal train, reflecting the quasi-periodic geodesic motion on $\Sigma_2$. We also comment on the generalization to wormhole mimickers of non-extremal black holes and on the implications of these results for unitarity in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence.
papers.comments: 33 pages; v3: more comments and references, to appear in Phys. Rev. D

papers.title: Nambu's Dynamics, Strings and Gravitized Quantum Theory
papers.abstract: In this article we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory. String theory, according to this view, originates in foundations of quantum theory and Nambu's dynamics, which features in the non-perturbative definition of string theory in terms of a T-duality covariant and non-commutative formulation, called the metastring. Nambu's dynamics and the associated cubic and hypercubic objects also appear as the natural language for exploring the new observables and phenomena implied by a dynamical Born rule, including triple and higher order quantum interference, that can be investigated in experiments involving massive quantum probes, and that are also needed for direct empirical tests of the Born rule, a cornerstone of quantum theory.

papers.title: The accretion flow and jet of M87: broadband modelling across spatial scales
papers.abstract: The nearby radio galaxy M87 is an ideal laboratory for studying accretion flows and relativistic jet emission. The EHT collaboration conducted the most comprehensive multi-wavelength observational campaign of M87, in which radio instruments with resolutions ranging from tens of microarcseconds to about an arcsecond sampled different portions of the outflow. We model these data using a radiatively inefficient accretion flow (RIAF) with winds and a new multi-zone jet model, initially magnetically dominated, in which we solve the transport equation for the non-thermal electrons as they are injected, advected, and cooled along the jet. We then compare each radio flux with the jet emission within an effective aperture set by the angular scale of the corresponding observation and obtain the best fit for the jet parameters. The comparison across spatial scales favours a scenario in which the RIAF, rather than the jet, produces the compact $230~{\rm GHz}$ emission, while the jet dominates the lower-frequency radio, optical/UV and X-ray emission. The Jet+RIAF model connects the Bondi-scale gas supply to an accretion rate at the horizon of ${\approx}10^{-5}$ of the Eddington rate, consistent with EHT polarimetry, and the two jets carry in total ${\approx}13$ per cent of the accretion power, $10^{43}~{\rm erg~s}^{-1}$. The framework presented in this work provides a simple way to disentangle the accretion-flow and jet contributions to the emission from nearby radio galaxies.
papers.comments: 18 pages, 9 figures, accepted in Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc

papers.title: The Milky Way's Early Disk Was Built in Bursts. II. The Multicomponent Age-Metallicity Structure of the High-$α$ Disk
papers.abstract: Whether the high-$\alpha$ disk experienced a continuous or episodic star-formation history remains an open question. Here we investigate the age--metallicity distribution of the high-$\alpha$ disk using approximately 145,000 Gaia DR3 subgiants with $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]>-1$, 6.5~kpc $\lesssim R\lesssim9.5$~kpc, and $|Z|\lesssim1.5$~kpc. We adopt a forward-modelling framework that accounts for individual age and metallicity uncertainties and corrects for sample selection effects. The reconstructed distribution reveals two components: a broad, dominant population peaking at $\sim10.6$ Gyr and $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]\simeq-0.38$, and an older, more metal-poor population peaking at $\sim12.4$ Gyr and $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]\simeq-0.79$. These features suggest an episodic history of star formation and chemical enrichment in the high-$\alpha$ disk, qualitatively consistent with cosmological simulations in which recurrent gas accretion drives variations in the star formation rate. The age of the older component is close to the $\sim12.3$~Gyr epoch inferred for the proposed Low-energy--Kraken--Heracles accretion event, suggesting a possible connection between this early interaction and enhanced disk star formation. There is tentative evidence that the dominant population is possibly composed of two sub-components with age distributions peaking at $\sim11.1$ Gyr and $\sim10.0$ Gyr, respectively. Together, these results favour a picture in which the high-$\alpha$ disk was built through recurrent episodes of enhanced star formation rather than a single temporally smooth phase, even for the regime of ${\rm [Fe/H]}>-1$.

papers.title: SpecLess: A Multi Survey Python Package for Machine Learning Classification of Galaxy Morphology and Activity from Photometry
papers.abstract: Galaxy morphology and spectroscopic activity are fundamental observational diagnostics of galaxy formation and evolution. However, the extent to which these properties can be recovered from broadband photometry and preserved across different sky surveys remains an important question. In this study, we use photometric data from KiDS+VIKING, the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys and SDSS+AllWISE to systematically investigate the complementary information provided by optical, near-infrared and mid-infrared wavelengths for galaxy classification. Our machine learning models achieve macro F1 scores of 0.9237 and 0.7398 for morphological and activity classification, respectively. We show that the contribution of near-infrared photometry varies across galaxy populations, yielding an improvement of 9.25 percentage points in the classification accuracy of red spiral galaxies. Controlled experiments on 5,235 galaxies common to KiDS+VIKING and DESI demonstrate that mid-infrared photometry provides greater complementary information for discriminating spectroscopic activity classes than additional optical measurements. Furthermore, cross-survey transfer experiments conducted on identical galaxies with fixed reference labels reveal direction-dependent performance losses in the generalizability of photometric classifiers. These findings demonstrate that the limitations of photometric galaxy classification are governed not only by the choice of algorithm but also by the physical properties of galaxy populations, wavelength coverage and catalogue-specific observational differences. As an outcome of this study, we present SpecLess, an open-source Python package providing survey-specific classifiers that require no spectroscopic information at inference.
papers.comments: 14 pages, 2 figures, 15 tables. Submitted. SpecLess v0.3.0. Open source Python package available at this https URL

papers.title: A no-go theorem for closed timelike curves in globally null-foliated spacetimes
papers.abstract: The study of closed timelike curves has proceeded one spacetime at a time, and the criteria available form three families, the time function criteria, the energy condition criteria and the topological criteria. We initiate a fourth family of criteria, elementary in form and resting on a single scalar equation rather than any energy condition. We prove that a spacetime admitting a globally defined function whose gradient is everywhere null and nonzero cannot contain a closed timelike curve, and that the hypothesis is logically independent of stable causality rather than weaker than it. The proof turns on one algebraic fact, that a null covector is never orthogonal to a timelike vector, so the function grows strictly along every timelike curve and cannot close. Because the null eikonal equation alone decides the criterion, we can use it where the classical time function theorem is silent. We establish for the first time that no Kundt spacetime and no Robinson--Trautman spacetime can contain a closed timelike curve on any region where the null coordinate is globally single valued, whatever the cosmological constant and the rotation one form, which settles a question left open for gyratonic waves. We further show that the Misner, Ori and Ahmed constructions contain closed timelike curves along coordinate circles that become timelike under the periodic identification, and that the cosmological constant, the expansion and the shear are spectators in all of them.
papers.comments: 39 pages, 2 figs. References added; the statement of the quotient criterion in Sec. VI.D is corrected; the main theorem and the main conclusions are unchanged

papers.title: Gravitational waves flooding the Universe after wall domination
papers.abstract: We discuss a possible early Universe scenario, where radiation era is interrupted by the epoch of domination of domain walls eventually annihilating into particles. During this period the Universe undergoes accelerated expansion, while the comoving correlation length of the domain wall network remains constant. The network serves as a source of tensor modes, which get frozen upon exiting the horizon similarly to the case of inflationary fluctuations. The modes re-enter the horizon during the subsequent stage of radiation domination and since then contribute to the gravitational wave background. The period of wall domination is manifested in the spectral shape of gravitational waves via a distinctive plateau replacing a peak, which is characteristic for the scenario with sub-dominant walls. The gravitational waves are strong enough to be observed with present-day and future facilities in a broad range of frequencies. In particular, their energy density is sufficient to produce a significant impact on the effective number of neutrino species, unless the duration of wall domination is suitably constrained.
papers.comments: 21 pages, 1 figure; minor improvements and clarifications added

papers.title: Multilayer magnetic structure toward NGC 1333 revealed by a square-degree optical polarimetric survey
papers.abstract: Magnetic-field studies of star-forming regions are complicated by overlapping structures along the line of sight. We investigate the large-scale magnetic field toward NGC~1333 in Perseus, accounting for foreground polarization through stellar distances and optical polarimetry. Our wide-field $R$-band survey covers nearly one square degree and provides polarization measurements for approximately 840 stars, with distances from Gaia DR3 and StarHorse. We used polarization-distance trends and Stokes parameters to identify line-of-sight components and estimate foreground polarization. After subtracting it in Stokes space, we characterized the field using circular statistics and the angular dispersion function (ADF), comparing it with molecular-line and complementary polarimetric observations. The data reveal a polarized foreground at 160-300 pc and a cloud component beyond 300 pc. After correction, the plane-of-sky field rotates smoothly from $126.3°\pm0.8°$ in the northwest to $162.2°\pm0.6°$ in the southeast, remaining well ordered in both regions. The ADF gives turbulent-to-ordered field ratios of $0.054^{+0.025}_{-0.022}$ and $0.095^{+0.021}_{-0.047}$, corresponding to plane-of-sky strengths of $59^{+44}_{-23}$ and $46^{+50}_{-13}~\mu\mathrm{G}$. Residual foreground fluctuations may affect these estimates. CO data show multiple velocity components with spatially varying contributions. Corrected optical polarization agrees with the large-scale orientation traced by Planck, while near-infrared and JCMT/POL-2 data reveal localized deviations in denser structures. Our results indicate a coherent cloud-scale magnetic field with a smoothly changing orientation, alongside localized variations in dense structures. They demonstrate the value of combining stellar distances and wide-field optical polarimetry to disentangle foreground contributions.

papers.title: An Orbital Curvature for ISCOs
papers.abstract: Building on the fact that circular orbits are the fixed points of the phase portraits arising from the geodesic equations on a black hole spacetime, we develop a general orbital geometry, which captures the stability structure of orbits. The construction uses the orbital energy, angular momentum and angular velocity as state space variables, with response functions encoding how the circular orbits react to changes in the black hole background and in their angular motion. The associated scalar curvature provides a geometric diagnostic of certain distinguished points of the circular orbit family, such as the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), where it becomes singular. Across the ISCO, the relevant orbital response functions change sign as the system passes from the stable to the unstable circular orbit branch, and are found to vanish at marginal stability. We illustrate the framework for Schwarzschild black holes in asymptotically flat four dimensions, and five dimensional Schwarzschild AdS spacetimes. In the four dimensional case, the ISCO is associated with a degeneration of the energy response sector, while in the five dimensional AdS case it is detected through the angular response. The AdS example also exhibits a separate curvature singularity at a point which coincides with the minimum temperature of the black hole background. These results show that the orbital geometry provides a promising unified framework for characterizing the stability of circular orbits and criticality of ISCOs.
papers.comments: 29 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. v2: clarifications and revised discussions with references added, typos corrected

papers.title: Spectral function, OPE, and QNMs detect different singular points of black branes with unequal R-charges
papers.abstract: We consider black brane solutions in the STU model, with three R-charges labeled by the parameters $q_1,q_2,q_3$. For equal R-charges $q_1=q_2=q_3$, the solution becomes the Reissner-Nordström black brane. For unequal R-charges $q_1>q_2>q_3\geq0$, there are three curvature singular points at $R\equiv r^2=-q_i$. Only $R=-q_3$ is the physical singularity, and the other two lie beyond it. Their optical times $T_i$, the complex times of null rays from the boundary to these singular points and back, form a right triangle in the complex $T$-plane. We probe these singular points using three observables, all built from the retarded correlator of $T_{xy}$ at zero spatial momentum: spectral function, OPE coefficients, and QNMs. The exponentially small correction to the spectral function at large real frequency is dominated by $T_1$ and $T_2$, which have the smallest ${\rm Im}\,T_i$. The OPE convergence radius is determined by $T_1$, which has the smallest $|T_i|$. A line of QNMs lies along the direction of $1/T_2$, since $T_2$ has the smallest phase $\arg T_i$. Furthermore, there is a second line of QNMs along the negative imaginary axis, which carries information about $T_3$ corresponding to the physical singularity. We derive these results from a WKB analysis and check them numerically. The three observables are therefore sensitive to different singular points of the geometry.
papers.comments: 45 pages, 8 figures; v2: references added, Sec. 4 expanded

papers.title: Angular momentum transport in a newborn protostar--disc system: magnetic braking, spiral arms and the magneto-rotational instability
papers.abstract: Angular momentum transport in young protostar--disc systems involves magnetic braking, magneto-rotational turbulence and gravitational instability, mechanisms that are usually studied separately and on different scales. We present a three-dimensional non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic simulation, including Ohmic and ambipolar diffusion, that follows the collapse of a $1~M_\odot$ dense core continuously from the cloud scale to the formation of the protostar, and then the resulting protostar--disc system for $\sim 64~\mathrm{yr}$ at a resolution of $\sim 10^{-4}~\mathrm{AU}$ at the protostellar surface. We decompose the azimuthally averaged angular momentum budget into Reynolds, Maxwell and gravitational torques, each split into a radial and a meridional component, over a quasi-steady phase of the evolution. The collapse produces a thick disc an order of magnitude more massive than the protostar, whose specific angular momentum decreases as it accretes. Accretion through the disc is vertically layered, with accreting and decreting layers at the same radius, a pattern set layer by layer by the torques. The transport separates into three regimes delimited by the coupling of the magnetic field to the gas. Magnetic braking operates in the envelope. Maxwell stresses dominate inside $\sim 0.1~\mathrm{AU}$, where the field recouples and the magneto-rotational instability develops. In the ambipolar dead zone that makes up the bulk of the disc, the Reynolds stress dominates, carried by $m=2$ spiral arms in a marginally unstable disc, with the gravitational stress as a secondary contributor. Meridional transport is as important as radial transport, so that a one-dimensional viscous model fitted to the net mass flux would require a negative $\alpha$ over part of the disc.
papers.comments: 27 pages, 27 figures, 1 table, submitted to Open Journal of Astrophysics

papers.title: Landau Theory of Black Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
papers.abstract: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.

papers.title: Unsupervised learning reveals a small number of galaxy formation pathways in IllustrisTNG
papers.abstract: Understanding the main drivers of galaxy formation and the connection between observable properties and evolutionary pathways is a central goal of extragalactic astronomy. Observations provide single-epoch snapshots of galaxies at different stages of their development, whereas cosmological simulations allow us to trace the full formation histories of individual systems within a theoretical framework. Extracting information from these datasets remains challenging. Our aim is to use machine-learning techniques to unveil physical properties from the simulation datasets. We apply two unsupervised ML techniques, dimensionality reduction and clustering, to identify galaxy evolution key parameters. We use UMAP as our dimensionality reduction tool and k-means as our clustering method. We perform dimensionality reduction on the star formation histories (SFHs) of a sample of aproximately 10000 galaxies drawn from the TNG50 and TNG100 simulations. The resulting representation of the SFHs in a two-dimensional UMAP space reveals a clear ordering of galaxy mass assembly histories, separating quenched and star-forming systems, as well as galaxies with significant ex situ stellar mass contributions. Galaxy properties from simulation catalogs that are not used in the dimensionality reduction show correlations across the UMAP plane. Furthermore, using a k-means clustering analysis, we identify six groups of galaxies with distinct evolutionary histories. These groups show systematic differences in stellar mass, morphology, angular momentum, star formation activity, and merger history, and occupy different regions of the SFR-mass and mass-size planes. Our results indicate that the diversity of galaxy formation histories in IllustrisTNG can be organized into a small number of characteristic evolutionary pathways linking galaxy accretion histories and present-day structural and star-forming properties.

papers.title: Transient Information in Moving-Mirror Quantum Correlations
papers.abstract: We study how a finite dynamical history remains encoded in a quantum field after a moving mirror returns to a common thermal trajectory. Two compact deformations of the Carlitz--Willey ray map are related by reversal of a control parameter and share the same asymptotic null line and Hawking temperature. The pairing induces an exact even--odd grading of the peeling field and Bogoliubov transformation. The complex continuum covariance retains the transient sign at first order, while the leading monochromatic quadratic response is even under reversal. Finite-bandwidth wave packets convert this distinction into signed interference with the thermal reference covariance. In linear response, the signed squared correlation is quartic in bandwidth for the selected right-moving packets and cubic for matched Rindler/Milne packets. The relative cross-covariance phase has a linear bandwidth dependence, with its leading coefficient maximized in magnitude by the flat window among normalized real symmetric windows. Finite-amplitude corrections introduce an additional linear bandwidth term in the squared Rindler/Milne response. The distinguishing packets sample the transient history in retarded time, while both trajectories share the same asymptotic Hawking temperature.
papers.comments: 11 pages, 3 figures; corrected author name in metadata

papers.title: Searching for Anisotropic Cosmic Birefringence with SPT-3G
papers.abstract: We search for anisotropic cosmic birefringence using two years of data from the SPT-3G instrument on the South Pole Telescope. Anisotropic cosmic birefringence refers to a theorized dependence of the refractive index of the vacuum on the polarization of light that varies across the Universe in a statistically isotropic manner. Such an effect would manifest as a direction-dependent mixing of the $E$ and $B$ polarization modes of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), caused by rotation of the polarization angle as photons travel from the CMB last scattering surface to us. We present a measurement of the power spectrum of the rotation angle $\alpha$ in six bins across the angular multipole range $20 < L < 2048$, finding no evidence for cosmic birefringence with the spectrum consistent with zero. At 95% confidence, we set a new best upper limit on the amplitude of a scale-invariant birefringence power spectrum of $A_{\rm CB}<0.027$. Additionally, we place upper limits on a scale-dependent white noise model. We translate the scale-invariant upper limit to constraints on the axion coupling constant and primordial magnetic field strength, finding 95% confidence limits of $g_{\alpha\gamma} < 1.7\times 10^{-2}/H_I$ and $B_{\rm 1\,Mpc} < 9.6\,{\rm nG}$ respectively. We expect these limits to improve several-fold with the complete SPT-3G survey.
